what_i_got_wrong:
TWO, and the second is the more useful one.
(1) The first version of the table parser broke on the markdown separator row `|---|---|---|---|` and returned an empty dict, so the new assertion fired its own `did not parse` guard rather than passing. Caught by running the test, not by reading it. That guard existing at all is why the failure was legible instead of a vacuous pass over an empty table — an empty parse must never read as agreement.
(2) ⛔ I WROTE THE LEDGER WITH MY OWN `json.dump(..., indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)` INSTEAD OF THE REPO'S PINNED WRITER, AND PREFLIGHT CAUGHT IT: `test_the_ledger_has_one_serialization.py::test_write_ledger_reproduces_the_committed_file_byte_for_byte` failed on the first run. This is AUT-PD-037's defect class exactly, and the guard filed for it did its job. Fixed by re-running `priority.py --write`, which routes through `ledger_io.write_ledger` — the one place the committed serialization is pinned. AUT-PD-163 survived the rewrite with its score and state intact; the serialization suite then passed 9/9. ⭐ THE LESSON IS NARROW AND WORTH STATING: a hand-filed ledger row must be written by re-running the ranker, never by a bespoke json.dump, because `indent=` and `ensure_ascii=` are pinned somewhere this cycle never opened.
(3) I wrote `subagents.max_concurrent: 0` into this receipt and then dispatched a seat, which would have made the receipt false in exactly the field `health.py`'s `fanout_is_governed` reads. Corrected before the commit, and the preflight run that was in flight against the old tree was KILLED rather than protected — an invalidated run is cheap and an idle wait is not (CLAUDE.md §6).

harness_exit_code_disagreed_with_the_mar: ⛔⛔ MEASURED THIS CYCLE, NOT INHERITED. The first preflight run was backgrounded, and the harness reported `completed (exit code 0)` while the log's own marker, written by `echo "EXIT=$?" >> log`, said `EXIT=1` — and the log's last line was `PREFLIGHT FAILED -- do not commit.` The marker was right and the harness was wrong. Committing on the harness's word would have pushed a ledger that fails the trunk's own serialization gate, on the very cycle whose whole subject is a guard that went unnoticed for five commits. This is the third rule in the cycle prompt and it is not theoretical: READ THE MARKER, NEVER THE REPORTED EXIT CODE.
